title: U.S. House · New York's 17th Congressional District
area: Lower Hudson Valley, covering Rockland and Putnam counties and parts of Westchester and Dutchess counties, north of New York City.

context.text: Cait Conley won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary over Beth Davidson, Effie Phillips-Staley, John Cappello, and Mike Sacks, 49.5% to 31.8% and lower totals for the others. Phillips-Staley separately won the Working Families Party primary but subsequently withdrew from the November general-election ballot; Conley is the WFP nominee as well as the Democratic nominee. Incumbent Michael Lawler advanced unopposed on the Republican and Conservative Party lines after his primary was canceled.

Lawler defeated then-incumbent Sean Patrick Maloney 50.3% to 49.7% in 2022 (under different district lines) and won re-election 52.1% to 45.8% in 2024, the same year Kamala Harris carried the district 49.9% to 49.3%. As of September 22, 2026, all four major forecasters (Cook Political Report, Decision Desk, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball) rated the general election a "Toss-up." As of June 30, 2026, Lawler had raised $8.17 million to Conley's $4.32 million.

summary.text: Mike Lawler is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for New York's 17th Congressional District, first elected in 2022 after one term in the New York State Assembly. Before public office he worked as a campaign and party staffer, a county executive's adviser and a town official, and he founded a government affairs and public relations firm. He sits on the House Financial Services and Foreign Affairs committees, and is running for re-election.

background.text: Born in Suffern, New York; lives in Pearl River with his wife, Doina, and their two daughters, according to his official biography.

Graduated from Manhattan College, where, according to his official biography, he earned degrees in accounting and finance and was class valedictorian; Ballotpedia lists a 2009 bachelor's degree from the college.

Early career: worked as a senior adviser in the office of Westchester County Executive Rob Astorino, served as executive director of the New York State Republican Party, and, per his official biography, founded a government affairs and public relations firm; Ballotpedia lists him as a partner with Checkmate Strategies.
Served as Deputy Town Supervisor of Orangetown, New York, before running for the State Assembly.
Represented New York's 97th Assembly District from 2021 to 2022, serving on the Aging, Banks, Education and Housing committees and as ranking member of Governmental Operations.
Elected to Congress in 2022, defeating incumbent Rep. Sean Maloney (D) 50.3%-49.7% under different district lines, and re-elected in 2024 with 52.1% of the vote to 45.8%.

In the House he serves on the Financial Services Committee, where he is Vice Chair of Communications, and on the Foreign Affairs Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on the Middle East and North Africa, according to his official biography.

His official biography says that in the 118th Congress he introduced 58 bills, 7 of which passed the House and 1 of which became law, and that he was a leading member of the bipartisan SALT Caucus whose work contributed to the higher State and Local Tax deduction cap enacted in 2025.

Co-chairs the Moldova Caucus, Anti-Congestion Tax Caucus, Appalachian National Scenic Trail Caucus and Extreme Heat Caucus, and is a member of more than 50 other caucuses, according to his official biography.

priorities.text: Campaign material emphasizes constituent service and a record he describes as bipartisan, citing additional funding for law enforcement and first responders, tax relief for middle-class families, and funding increases for Hudson Valley schools he says he secured in the state Assembly.
priorities.quote: In the Assembly, that meant additional funding for law enforcement and first responders, tax relief for middle class families, and historic funding increases for our schools in the Hudson Valley.

priorities.text: Says he has opposed New York City congestion pricing as a tax on Hudson Valley commuters.
priorities.quote: Led the fight against Gov. Hochul's absurd congestion pricing plan – a $5,000/year commuter tax on hardworking Hudson Valley families just trying to get to work

positions.summary: Has campaigned against Manhattan congestion pricing as a policy imposed on Hudson Valley commuters and taxpayers.

record.text: Serves on the House Financial Services Committee (Capital Markets and Housing and Insurance subcommittees) and, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026), chairs the House Foreign Affairs Committee's Middle East and North Africa Subcommittee and also sits on its Western Hemisphere Subcommittee.
Represented the 97th District in the New York State Assembly from 2021 to 2023 before his election to Congress.

summary.text: Cait Conley is a U.S. Army veteran and former White House National Security Council and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency official, running as the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for NY-17. She grew up in the Hudson Valley, attended West Point and served 16 years in the Army before federal national security roles in the Biden administration. She won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, and describes herself as not a politician.

background.text: According to her campaign website, she is a fourth-generation Hudson Valley native whose mother was a postal worker and whose father was a construction worker, and she attended Pine Bush High School.

Her campaign website says she began her application to the U.S. Military Academy at West Point after the September 11 attacks, received a congressional nomination from the late Rep. Maurice Hinchey, and was the first in her family to graduate from college.
Earned a bachelor's degree from West Point and master's degrees from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Harvard University.

Served 16 years as an active-duty Army officer, starting as a military police officer and later in special operations leadership; according to her campaign website, she deployed overseas six times to combat zones including Iraq and Afghanistan and was awarded three Bronze Stars.

Served as Director for Counterterrorism on the National Security Council at the White House and later at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) under President Joe Biden, according to her campaign website and Ballotpedia.
Her campaign website says that in these roles she worked with Congress on national security legislation and on the security of critical infrastructure and election systems.
Lives in Millwood, according to a June 2026 River Journal candidate profile.

priorities.text: Campaign website lists education investment (affordable childcare, universal pre-K, capping student-loan interest rates, opposing voucher programs) and rebuilding aging infrastructure as priorities.

positions.summary: Opposes voucher programs, saying they strip funding from public education.
Supports increasing access to affordable childcare through federal subsidies and tax credits and investing in universal pre-K.

researchNotes: Effie Phillips-Staley won the June 23 Working Families Party primary but withdrew from the November general-election ballot and is not included here; Cait Conley holds the WFP line as well as the Democratic line. Neither Lawler nor Conley had completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey as of research date; their priorities and positions draw on campaign-website material republished by Ballotpedia. Biographical details for Conley come largely from her campaign website and a candidate questionnaire profile; her campaign materials do not list her birth year.
